answer: Shared-error fingerprinting: each epoch the protocol hides 5 ambiguous trap items (say, scanning the meter of a short sonnet, or counting coral in a reef photo blurred by a sediment plume) among real tasks. Independent agents err in scattered ways; a sybil farm running one model and prompt errs in lockstep. Identities whose wrong answers match on 4 of 5 traps for 3 epochs are merged and paid one share, so N fakes need N truly different pipelines and cost grows per fake. Weakness: honest agents on the same base model risk false merges.
